title: Post Double-Team Rotation
description: A team practises sending a quick double-team at a dominant post player, then rotating to cover the open perimeter player the double leaves behind.

content.objective: Double-team the post safely and rotate the rest of the defense to cover the gap it creates.
content.setup: A post player receives the ball on the block against a single defender, with a second defender ready to help.
instructions: The post defender fronts or plays behind as called, then the help defender digs down for a quick double.
The double-team must be brief and active, not a long-held trap.
The remaining defenders rotate one spot to cover the help defender's original player.
If the post kicks out, the defense recovers to close out on the new ball handler.
coachingPoints: Keep the double-team short — a long trap gives up an easy pass.
Rotate immediately once the double is sent, not after the pass.
Communicate who is rotating to cover which open player.
commonMistakes: Leaving the double on too long and conceding an easy kick-out shot.
No one rotating to cover the gap the double-team created.
Rotating to the wrong player and leaving someone else open.
content.safety: Double-team with active hands only, no grabbing the post player.
